newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-MPs stall decision on pensions equality rules.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs stall decision on pensions equality rules.

text.p: The European Parliament stalled its decision on Wednesday on a proposal for equal treatment of men and women in pension provisions.

Euro-MPs adopted the first 13 of 14 amendments proposed by Portuguese Socialist Helena Torres Marques, and rejected the last one, only to hear from European Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler that the Commission could accept only amendment 5.
On hearing this, the plenary voted to return the proposal to committee.

The vote, under the consultation procedure, related to European Commission proposal COM(95)186 to amend Directive 86/378/EEC on the equal treatment of men and women in occupational social security schemes.
The Commission said it could not accept the other amendments which the rapporteur said were intended to remove proposed changes which would have penalised female workers.

Torres Marques said her amendments would have allowed for more flexible pension arrangements, guaranteed actuarial "equivalence" in calculating men and womens' pensions and would have included part-time workers.
